description: Issue #181: a literal companion is granted VERBATIM, so it is the one companion shape whose safety no placeholder can guarantee. A `derive` add is built out of a declared path, which extraction already refused to invent outside the repository; a `require` add is whatever the profile wrote. `users/kewton/notes/shared-contract.test.mjs` is the shape an author produces by pasting an absolute path and deleting the leading slash — it is repository-relative in form and outside the repository in fact, so it must be refused at profile load (load_error, exit 6) before an issue is read. The path is chosen so that ONLY the safety predicate can be refusing it (§15.8's lesson from case 46): `..`, a leading `/` and a backslash are all caught by the template parser instead, and a fixture that trips two checks measures neither. Drop the `isSafeRepoPath` call from the literal branch and this case is the one that goes red.
